system.name: ELIT
system.one_liner: Drop-in diffusion-transformer mechanism: a variable-length latent interface with Read/Write cross-attention lets the number of latents set the compute budget.

content.variant_note: three tiles in one row read as an equation: a minimal DiT + ELIT sketch, a quality-FLOPs scatter, and a sample grid at shrinking budgets beside the baseline
content.argues: A variable-length latent interface lets one DiT-style model trade quality for FLOPs smoothly: ELIT curves beat the baselines and samples degrade gracefully as the budget shrinks.
content.subject: Sketch of DiT blocks with Latent Interface, Read and Write; FDD-vs-GFLOPs scatter for three backbones; text-to-image samples at shrinking budgets next to the full-budget baseline.

new_tags.name: equation-header

lessons.what_to_learn: Keep one colour pair (blue baseline, red ours) from a tiny architecture sketch through the result plot to the frames and titles of the sample grid, and head the strip with 'A + B =' so three unlike tiles read as one claim. Show a budget as one arrow with FLOPs share and token count under samples that step through it.
lessons.suits: Teasers for plug-in mechanisms (efficiency, adapters, schedulers) where a minimal sketch, a trade-off plot and a strip of samples together make the case.

evidence: At inference, the number of latent tokens is a user-controlled knob that yields a smooth quality–FLOPs trade-off
Read pulls information from input tokens, which we will refer to as spatial, into the latent interface
Write broadcasts updated latents back to the spatial tokens.

summary: ELIT (Elastic Latent Interface Transformer) is a drop-in addition to diffusion transformers that inserts a variable-length set of latent tokens plus two cross-attention layers, Read and Write, so the compute per step is set by the number of latents instead of the image size. Figure 1 is a teaser in three tiles under an equation header 'DiT + ELIT = Flexible Compute Allocation': a minimal sketch of three groups of DiT Blocks with the Latent Interface strip, Read and Write; an FDD-versus-GFLOPs scatter in which red ELIT curves for DiT, U-ViT and HDiT sit below single blue baseline points; and a 3 x 6 grid of text-to-image samples at shrinking budgets (35% to 69% of the FLOPs, 320 to 4096 tokens) beside the full-budget Qwen-Image column. Blue means baseline and red means ELIT throughout.
summary_zh: ELIT 给 DiT 加上可变长度的潜变量接口和 Read/Write 交叉注意力，靠潜变量数控制算力。图 1 由三块组成：结构草图、FDD-GFLOPs 散点图、不同预算下的文生图样例，蓝色为基线，红色为 ELIT。
notes: Prior labels kept (contribution-mosaic first). The digest calls the font sans, but the preview shows serif labels at 7 pt and sans plot text at 4 pt. The sketch has no arrows; the heads counted in the digest are the triangle markers of the plot plus the budget arrow. The 69% label sits under the 4096-token column, which is not explained in the figure.
